findings.title: getClientsWithPermission adds the literal resource type name to the granted set
findings.body: In ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission, the lambda passed to resourceStore.findByType iterates over every resource with type "Clients", including the "Clients" resource itself (the all-clients resource whose name is the string "Clients"). When the caller has any scope permission on that all-clients resource, hasGrantedPermission returns true and the code does granted.add(resource.getName()), which inserts the literal string "Clients" into the set. "Clients" is not a valid client internal id (UUID), so any consumer that uses the returned set to look up or filter clients (e.g. comparing against ClientModel.getId()) will get an empty result and silently break filtering for callers who have only the all-clients permission. The "Clients" resource itself must be excluded (e.g. skip when resource.getName().equals(AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)).

findings.title: Event listener gate allows V1 path to call V2 code that throws
findings.body: The listener is wrapped in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))`, but inside it the code calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(...). The static management() helper returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, regardless of the V1 flag. After this PR, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled now throws UnsupportedOperationException. So when both V1 and V2 feature flags are enabled and a client is removed, the listener still fires (V1 gate passes) and the call into ClientPermissionsV2 throws. Roles/groups don't have this problem because MgmtPermissionsV2 inherits their V1 implementations, but the client branch does. The gate needs to be "V1 enabled AND V2 not enabled", or the listener must dispatch through a V1-only helper, otherwise client deletion can blow up at runtime in deployments with both flags on.

findings.title: getResourceName ignores the new Clients resource type
findings.body: getResourceName handles USERS specially: it resolves the resource to "All users" for the type resource and to user.getUsername() for individual user resources. There is no branch for the new CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, so the method silently falls through to return resource.getDisplayName(). Because clients are stored with resource.getName() == client.getId() (the internal UUID produced by resolveClient), the value returned for any client-related policy/resource will be an opaque UUID rather than the human-readable clientId (e.g. "myclient"). UI/admin displays that rely on getResourceName will show UUIDs for clients while showing usernames for users, which is inconsistent and not user-friendly. Add an else-if branch for CLIENTS that returns "All clients" for the type resource and client.getClientId() (looked up from session.clients()) otherwise.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission is not covered by tests
findings.body: The PR introduces the override ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission(String), but no test exercises it. The closest coverage (testViewAllClients) only checks findAll() visibility, which can succeed via the all-clients role check without ever calling getClientsWithPermission. Without a dedicated test that calls getClientsWithPermission("view"/"manage") for an admin who has only the all-clients permission and asserts that the returned set contains the right client ids and does not contain the literal "Clients", the bug at ClientPermissionsV2.java:138 (the all-clients resource being included in the result) cannot be caught by CI.

findings.title: Potential NullPointerException when "all-clients" resource is missing
findings.body: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...). getResourceTypeResource returns null in two cases: when supportsAuthorizationSchema(...) is false, and when the ResourceStore has no row with name == resource type (e.g. if AdminPermissionsSchema.init() never ran for this realm, or was upgraded in an unexpected order). The very next statement, authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource), then dereferences the possibly-null resource. This is reachable on any code path that asks for permission on a client before the schema initialization has produced the "Clients" resource. Guard with a null check (return false) before calling findByResource.
